les: Geloof en wins: twee redes om te vaar
kaps_punt: Die verspreiding van die Christelike godsdiens; Handel en wins maak

items.bewering: 'n Lang seereis het baie geld gekos en konings en ryk handelaars het daarvoor betaal.
items.bron: Wikipedia, '2nd Portuguese India Armada (Cabral, 1500)' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2nd_Portuguese_India_Armada_(Cabral,_1500)): most ships belonged to the Portuguese crown, the Anunciada was 'financed by an Italian consortium'; Wikipedia, 'Bartolomeo Marchionni' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bartolomeo_Marchionni): Florentine merchants in Lisbon provided capital for most early India voyages; da Gama's 1497 voyage was funded by the Crown and private merchants. Volledige soektog, hierdie rondte.

items.bewering: Hulle het verskeie redes gehad. Twee groot redes was geloof en wins.
items.bron: Review by Alexander Ponsen of Marcocci, 'A consciência de um império' (e-Journal of Portuguese History, Brown University, issue 24) and Teixeira and Lázaro (2025), as summarised in search results: religion and commerce are the two motives the historiography debates; other aims also existed (Prester John, crusade against Islam, a Christian kingship of Jerusalem for Manuel I - Britannica 'Manuel I', https://www.britannica.com/biography/Manuel-I). 'Verskeie redes' with 'twee groot redes' is accurate.

items.bewering: Die konings en die kerk van hulle tyd wou hê dat die Christelike geloof na ander dele van die wêreld gaan. Hulle het gehoop om mense daar tot hulle eie geloof te bring.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Inter caetera' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inter_caetera): the 1493 bull aims that 'barbarous nations be overthrown and brought to the faith itself' and exhorts the monarchs to spread the faith; Romanus Pontifex (1455) tied Portuguese expansion to the Christian mission (doctrineofdiscovery.org); Columbus's journal prologue (Las Casas copy, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Columbus%27s_journal) records the monarchs sending him to learn how to convert the people 'to our holy faith'; Cabral was commissioned to bring Christianity where he went.

items.bewering: Priesters het daarom saam met die seevaarders op die skepe gevaar.
items.bron: Wikipedia, '2nd Portuguese India Armada (Cabral, 1500)': 'the fleet carried eight Franciscan friars and eight chaplains', described as the first Portuguese Christian missionaries to India, sent to preach; New Advent Catholic Encyclopedia 'Pedralvarez Cabral' (https://www.newadvent.org/cathen/03128a.htm). No source named a priest on da Gama's first voyage, but the lesson's sentence is general and does not name a voyage.

items.bewering: Handel is wanneer mense goedere of dienste uitruil: deur te ruil, of deur te koop en te verkoop.
items.blok: Handel en wins as 'n groot rede
items.bron: Merriam-Webster 'trade' and Vocabulary.com 'trade' (https://www.vocabulary.com/dictionary/trade): buying and selling of goods and services, and exchange of one thing for another (barter).

items.bewering: Speserye soos peper, kaneel en naeltjies het van ver in die Ooste gekom.
items.blok: Handel en wins as 'n groot rede
items.bron: Purdue horticulture lecture (https://www.hort.purdue.edu/NEWCROP/hort_403/pp_pdf/pp_36.pdf): black pepper indigenous to the Malabar coast of India; cinnamon native to Sri Lanka; cloves native to the Moluccas (Ternate, Tidore, Bacan) - all in South and Southeast Asia.

items.bewering: Fyn stowwe soos sy het ook uit die Ooste gekom.
items.blok: Handel en wins as 'n groot rede
items.bron: Bedford/Macmillan 'Goods in Transit' (https://digfir-published.macmillanusa.com/strayer3e/strayer3e_ch7_6.html) and FIT exhibition 'Silk' (https://exhibitions.fitnyc.edu/fabric-in-fashion/silk/): Chinese silk travelled west; European traders imported expensive silks from the Far and Middle East. Note: by the 1400s Italy also wove silk, but the lesson does not say silk was not made in Europe, so the sentence stands.

items.bewering: Hierdie speserye het nie in Europa gegroei nie.
items.blok: Handel en wins as 'n groot rede
items.bron: Same sources as the origins item: pepper, cinnamon and cloves are tropical plants native to India, Sri Lanka and the Moluccas respectively; none was grown in Europe.

items.bewering: In Europa het hierdie goedere baie geld gekos en handelaars het 'n groot wins daaruit gemaak.
items.blok: Handel en wins as 'n groot rede
items.bron: Marketplace interview with food historian Michael Krondl (https://www.marketplace.org/story/2007/11/21/how-spices-became-acquired-taste): middlemen 'were making the real money', Venetians perhaps 40 percent, pepper sold in London for about 20 times its price at source.

items.bewering: Dink aan 'n sak peper op sy lang pad na Europa. Die boer wat dit gekweek het, het dit aan 'n handelaar verkoop.
items.blok: Hoekom peper in Europa so duur was
items.bron: Kerala Agricultural University chapter on North Malabar pepper (Cambridge Core, https://www.cambridge.org/core/product/identifier/CBO9788175968820A019/type/BOOK_PART): pepper 'cultivated from time immemorial' on the Malabar coast, trained by farmers on standard trees. Krondl notes some pepper was also foraged wild; a farmer who grew it is a fair illustrative case.

items.bewering: Daardie handelaar het dit oor die see geneem en ander het dit oor land verder gedra.
items.blok: Hoekom peper in Europa so duur was
items.bron: World History Encyclopedia, 'Middle Eastern Power Shifts & the Trade of Pepper from East to West' (https://www.worldhistory.org/article/1826/middle-eastern-power-shifts--the-trade-of-pepper-f/): pepper went by sea to the Red Sea or Persian Gulf, overland through Egypt or the Levant, then by Venetian ship from Alexandria. The sentence gives the sea-then-land order correctly; it omits the final Mediterranean sea leg, which makes it incomplete but not false, since 'verder' does not claim the land leg reached Europe.

items.bewering: Elke handelaar op die pad het die sak duurder verkoop en so sy eie wins gevat. Daarom het peper in Europa baie meer gekos as op die plek waar dit gegroei het. 'n Skip wat die speserye self daar kon gaan koop, kon baie van daardie hande oorslaan en veel meer wins maak.
items.blok: Hoekom peper in Europa so duur was
items.bron: Mapping checked: the chain of hands, each adding a markup, maps onto the documented route (Krondl, Marketplace: 'originally it was the middle man who were making the real money', pepper ~20x dearer in London than at source; the Portuguese and Dutch went direct 'to cut out the middle men'; World History Encyclopedia: Portugal's expansion 'driven by the pursuit of direct access to the spice markets of Asia'). Where a learner might reason further it does not mislead: skipping the hands also skips the customs duties levied along the way (e.g. Mamluk duties at Alexandria), which only strengthens the conclusion. The duties are an unmentioned additional cause, an omission rather than a false contrast. The block's comparatives ('baie meer', 'veel meer') are comparatives, not superlatives, and are supported.

items.bewering: Die twee redes het nie apart geloop nie. 'n Koning wat 'n reis betaal het, het gewoonlik albei redes genoem. Hy wou sy geloof versprei en hy wou wins maak.
items.bron: Da Gama's men at Calicut, 1498: 'We came in search of Christians and spices' (Roteiro, Modern History Sourcebook translation, University of Delaware, https://www1.udel.edu/History-old/figal/Hist104/assets/pdf/readings/01dagama.pdf); Cabral's 1500 commission joined lasting trade ties with spreading Christianity; Manuel I sought both the spice trade and a Christian alliance against Islam (Britannica 'Manuel I'); Columbus's prologue names conversion while the monarchs' investment aimed at Asian trade. Ponsen's review of Marcocci describes religion and commerce as 'mutually constitutive' in Portugal's expansion.

items.bewering: Ons kan vandag nie sê watter een van die twee die ware rede was nie.
items.bron: Ponsen's review of Marcocci (e-Journal of Portuguese History, Brown University) and Teixeira and Lázaro (2025), as summarised: most research has stressed economic motives, others foreground religion, and recent work treats the two as mutually constitutive. Historians still disagree on which was primary, so the claim that it cannot be settled matches the state of the historiography.

items.bewering: Hierdie twee redes help wys hoekom iemand bereid was om vir 'n lang reis te betaal. Hulle is 'n deel van die verhaal van die reise en nie die hele verhaal nie.
items.bron: Britannica 'Manuel I' and the Teixeira and Lázaro summary: other motives also figured (searching for Prester John, crusade against Islam, royal prestige), so 'not the whole story' is accurate.

items.bewering: Die res van hierdie onderwerp volg die Europese skepe op hulle pad verby die suidpunt van Afrika.
items.bron: 'Suidpunt' read as a superlative (southernmost point). Cape Agulhas is Africa's southernmost point; Dias passed it in 1488 and later fleets sailed past it into the Indian Ocean (amusingplanet.com 'Cape Agulhas', https://www.amusingplanet.com/2014/12/cape-agulhas-place-where-two-oceans-meet.html; Austria-Forum 'South Africa Cape of Good Hope', https://austria-forum.org/af/Geography/Africa/South_Africa/Special_Information/South_Africa_Cape_of_Good_Hope). The lesson does not name the Cape of Good Hope as the tip, so it avoids the common error. What the rest of the topic covers is a statement about the course, not a fact claim.

items.bewering: handel: Handel is wanneer mense goedere of dienste uitruil: deur te ruil, of deur te koop en te verkoop.
items.bron: Merriam-Webster and Vocabulary.com 'trade': buying and selling goods and services, or exchanging one thing for another.

items.bewering: wins: Wins is die geld wat oorbly nadat iemand al sy koste uit sy verkoopprys betaal het.
items.bron: Standard definition: profit = revenue minus costs (Merriam-Webster 'profit': the excess of returns over expenditure). The wording matches net profit, which is the everyday sense.

items.bewering: speserye: Droë dele van plante wat aan kos 'n sterk geur gee.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Spice' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spice): any seed, fruit, root, bark or other plant substance primarily used for flavouring or colouring food, generally dried; legal definitions call spices 'dried, pungent or aromatic substances of edible plant origin'. A few spices, such as ginger, are also used fresh, but 'dried' is the normal defining feature and the definition is not false.

opsomming: All 19 claims are confirmed against sources, including the one superlative ('suidpunt van Afrika') and the pepper-chain comparison, which maps correctly but leaves out customs duties as a second cause of the high price (incomplete, not false).
